svg.title: FormalSLT scope frontier
svg.desc: Two-column diagram showing what FormalSLT covers (verified) versus what it does not cover (open targets).
svg.text: FormalSLT scope frontier
Verified Lean 4 theorems versus open targets, as of the public release
In scope (verified, axiom-clean)
v Finite-class ERM + symmetrization
E[genGap] <= 2 E[Rad]; Massart B sqrt(2 log card(H) / n)
v Sharp McDiarmid via conditional sub-Gaussian engine
2 exp(-2 eps^2 / sum c_k^2), upper, lower, two-sided; homogeneous iid product
v VC + Sauer-Shelah binary route
(e n / d)^d growth; binary VC bridge; closed sample-complexity theorem
v Tight PAC-Bayes change of measure
Donsker-Varadhan, Catoni bound, McAllester grid peeling on bounded loss
v Finite contraction + linear predictors
Rad(phi o F) <= L Rad(F); Rad <= R/n sqrt(sum ||x_i||^2)
v Finite Dudley + total-bounded boundary adapters
Finite chains, dyadic schedules, separable-terminal Dudley boundary
v Algorithmic stability + Bousquet-Elisseeff
Bounded-differences scaffold, measure-theoretic iid product, Azuma-constant high prob
v Localized Bernstein finite scaffold (variance localization)
Out of scope (open targets)
o Continuous Dudley entropy integral
Library proves discrete chaining and boundary adapters; measure-theoretic integral remains
o Continuous-posterior PAC-Bayes (all-real-lambda)
Finite-grid peeling proved; uncountable-family change of measure is future work
o Anytime-valid sequential PAC-Bayes
Sub-gamma confidence sequences are out of the static finite-sample track
o Mathlib MGF unification
Sub-Gaussian and Bernstein MGF currently sit in separate FormalSLT modules
o General VC bridge for real-valued loss classes
Binary trace is proved; arbitrary real-valued VC requires effective-class extension
o Heterogeneous-product sharp McDiarmid
General theorem is over homogeneous iid product; per-coordinate distinct laws is a target
o Neural-network parameter-space generalization
Requires norm-controlled function classes, compression, or margin; not in the current spine
o VC-to-PAC full equivalence (lower bounds)
Verification standard: all in-scope items have at least one named axiom-clean Lean theorem with `#print axioms` checked.
Out-of-scope items are signposted in the README and in docs/assumptions-and-nonclaims.md; not vapor work.
